lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: slope as rate of change

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Find the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (6, 11).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt:
A line passes through these points:
x: 11, 13, 15
y: -9, -6, -3
What is the slope (rate of change) of the line?

A line passes through (3, -9). A slope triangle on the line has a horizontal leg (run) of 1 and a vertical leg (rise) of -2. A similar slope triangle further along the same line is 5 times as large. Which point also lies on the line?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A line has a slope of -9. A right triangle drawn along the line has a vertical leg (rise) of 26 units. What is the length of the other leg?
Write the equation, in slope-intercept form, of a line with slope 4/5 and y-intercept 12.
Identify the slope and y-intercept of the line y = (12/5)x + 3.

Relationship A: y = (7/4)x
Relationship B (proportional):
x: 1, 2, 3
y: 1, 2, 3
By how much does the greater rate of change exceed the lesser rate of change?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: For the line y = (4/3)x, find y when x = -11.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A line has equation y = (-12/5)x + 12. Which of these equations represents a line parallel to it?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
